answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: a network-wide registration faucet, refilling slowly, with priority by bid. New identities mint from one shared bucket whose kernel refills at a fixed trickle; a lone joiner, a single sparrow, rides the free trickle at no cost. To register faster you bid burned value per slot. A fleet wanting a thousand identities cannot summon them in one sable rush: it waits out the trickle serially or outbids for every slot, so mass creation is throttled network-wide. Honest arrival stays cheap; bulk arrival pays in time or burn, per identity.
